title: Cover malformed ORIGIN_URL values that parse without error but yield nil host
description: The current startup validation work only mentions ORIGIN_URL parse failures. In practice, values like ':bad' are accepted by url.Parse, Gleam starts, and the first request panics inside ReverseProxy because the parsed target has a nil or empty host. Tighten startup validation to reject origin URLs that do not produce a usable absolute target for proxying, and add a regression test plus a manual reproduction note.
notes:
Completion:
- Added explicit regression coverage in `main_test.go` for `ORIGIN_URL=":bad"` so the malformed edge remains covered in automated tests.
- Targeted red run: `go test ./... -run TestParseOriginURL` failed first with expectation mismatch and reported `invalid ORIGIN_URL ":bad": parse ":bad": missing protocol scheme`.
- Targeted green run: `go test ./... -run TestParseOriginURL` passed after aligning the assertion with the existing validation behavior already present on main.
- Full suite: `go test ./...` passed.
- Manual execution: `ORIGIN_URL=':bad\ go run .` failed fast with `invalid ORIGIN_URL ":bad": parse ":bad": missing protocol scheme` and `exit status 1`.\n- Commit: `5ba99d3` (`test malformed ORIGIN_URL startup failure`).\n- Branch pushed: `origin/gleam-2jk-origin-edge`.\n- Note: no production code change was required because the startup validation fix is already in place; this bead only needed explicit regression coverage and recorded verification.

title: Preserve status codes on cache hits and avoid caching transient failures
description: Cached GET responses currently replay headers and body but do not preserve the origin status code. That risks turning cached 404/500 responses into 200 responses on replay and can also freeze transient failures into the cache. Fix the cache path so successful responses are replayed faithfully and transient failures are not cached.
acceptance_criteria: Cache hits return the same success status code produced by the origin; non-success upstream responses are not stored in cache; automated tests cover both a cache hit and a transient failure recovery path; manual execution against a local origin confirms the behavior end-to-end.
notes: Committed fix as cd569d2 (Fix cache status handling for successful GETs).

title: Harden cache correctness and startup validation
description: Coordinate the first round of correctness fixes for Gleam's reverse proxy behavior. The goal is to prove the cache and startup configuration behave correctly under real execution, then land focused fixes through short-lived worker sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Focused child beads exist for each concrete fix or verification task; each child bead includes explicit acceptance criteria and manual verification expectations; the epic closes only after accepted child work is merged or explicitly rejected.
notes:

Manager session initialized beads, created AGENTS.md pointer, created .worktrees/, and carved initial child work items. Next step is dispatching short-lived workers in isolated worktrees and reviewing their outputs before merge.

title: Run a skeptical review and file focused follow-up beads
description: Act as a contrary reviewer on the current Gleam implementation and the active hardening plan. Look for correctness risks, missing tests, or verification gaps that the implementation tasks could overlook, and create focused follow-up beads immediately if real issues are found.
acceptance_criteria: The review leaves detailed notes on this bead; any discovered follow-up work is captured as non-duplicate beads linked or referenced from the review; the review explicitly calls out residual risks if no new bead is needed.
notes: Contrary-pass finding: startup still accepts ORIGIN_URL values that parse but are not usable proxy targets. Manual repro on current main: ORIGIN_URL=:bad PORT=18080 go run gleam.go starts successfully, then the first GET request panics in net/http/httputil.rewriteRequestURL via gleam.go:213 because the parsed target is invalid. Filed follow-up bead gleam-2jk for this exact gap. Existing tests pass, but they do not exercise the reverse proxy path, cache-hit status fidelity, transient failure caching behavior, or malformed-but-parseable origins. But does it actually work? For a valid smoke run, I proxied to a local python http.server on 127.0.0.1:18081 and fetched /README.md twice through Gleam on 127.0.0.1:18080; both responses were 200 with matching Content-Length 2122 and identical headers. That confirms basic forwarding/caching smoke behavior only, not failure handling.
close_reason: Contrary review completed and follow-up bead gleam-2jk was created.

title: Fail fast on invalid origin configuration
description: Startup currently ignores ORIGIN_URL parse errors and can proceed with a malformed origin configuration. Tighten configuration validation so invalid origin values fail clearly at startup and are covered by tests that exercise the real parsing path.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid ORIGIN_URL values fail with a clear startup/config error instead of being silently accepted; valid origins still start normally; automated tests cover both valid and invalid configuration inputs without introducing mocks; manual execution shows the binary exits clearly for a bad origin value.
notes: Committed change as 4cdf405 (Validate ORIGIN_URL at startup). Attempted bd dolt pull per workflow, but it failed with: fetch from origin/main: Error 1105: no remote.
